run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T22:11:06Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend is explained by frontend's own error spans between 22:11 and 22:18 UTC: its GET /api/data and POST /api/checkout requests returned HTTP 500, with error details showing gRPC UNAVAILABLE / ECONNREFUSED to the ad Service ClusterIP 100.65.180.246:8080 (grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds) and, via checkout, to the payment Service ClusterIP 100.70.188.60:8080 (oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge). Deployments ad and payment both carry kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T22:09:32Z and their pods were replaced at 22:09:32-22:09:36; ad produced no spans 22:12-22:18 and payment no spans 22:12-22:13, which matches those connections being refused. The ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config currently holds two enabled fault-injection settings naming exactly these two workloads, adFailure (variant on, "Fail ad service") and paymentFailure (variant 100%, "Fail payment service charge requests n%"); no other object was seen injecting a fault into ad or payment, so I name that ConfigMap the root-cause candidate, with the deployment restart and the resulting frontend 500s as its mechanism and consequences. This is partial: I did not observe the declared app-level faults (ad logged normal targeted-ad responses and payment logged "Transaction complete" once they were serving again, while the flags remained on), and I cannot tell when the ConfigMap settings changed or who applied the restart, because change history is not integrated.

claims.text: frontend's own error spans rose from 0 at 21:48-22:10 UTC to 0.13-0.85 spans/s at 22:11-22:18 UTC and returned to 0 at 22:19-22:21 UTC; the erroring operations were GET /api/data (identical series to grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds) and POST /api/checkout (identical series to grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder).

frontend error spans for grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds carry grpc.error_message "14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080" (rpc.grpc.status_code=14), and its GET /api/data spans returned http.status_code=500.

frontend POST /api/checkout spans returned http.status_code=500 with exception.message "13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card: ... rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = \"transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused\"", and checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge span failed with rpc.grpc.status_code=14.
The refused addresses are the Kubernetes Services ad (clusterIP 100.65.180.246, port 8080) and payment (clusterIP 100.70.188.60, port 8080).

Deployment ad has pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T22:09:32Z (generation 2, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad) and Deployment payment has kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T22:09:32Z (generation 2, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment); neither container defines readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe.

Events in otel-demo show Deployment/ad scaling ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0 and ad-6cb57f76d from 0 to 1 with pod ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 created and started at 22:09:32-22:09:35Z, and Deployment/payment scaling payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0 and payment-9c8ffb665 from 0 to 1 with pod payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 created and started at 22:09:32-22:09:36Z.

ad's span rate fell to 0 for 22:12-22:18 UTC after 0.9-1.6 spans/s up to 22:11 UTC and resumed at 1.77 spans/s at 22:19 UTC; payment's span rate was 0 at 22:12-22:13 UTC after ~0.5-0.9 spans/s and resumed at 1.23 spans/s at 22:14 UTC.

The restarted pods are currently Running, Ready and have restartCount 0: ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 (podIP 100.96.4.142, started 22:09:32Z) and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 (podIP 100.96.4.221, started 22:09:32Z); the ad and payment Endpoints currently list exactly these two pod IPs.

ad's container log shows normal request handling from 22:18:28-22:18:58 UTC ("Targeted ad request received for [books]" etc., "Non-targeted ad request received, preparing random response.") with no error lines in the 276 lines read for 22:05-22:20 UTC.

payment's container log shows normal processing ("Charge request received." followed by "Transaction complete.") from 22:13:22-22:13:57 UTC and again from 22:18:05-22:19:01 UTC, with no failure lines.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) contains enabled fault-injection settings: adFailure with defaultVariant "on" and description "Fail ad service"; paymentFailure with defaultVariant "100%" and description "Fail payment service charge requests n%"; the other flags including adHighCpu, adManualGc, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure, productCatalogFailure are defaultVariant "off".

The fault-injection settings held in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (adFailure on, paymentFailure 100%) are the root cause: they name exactly the two workloads whose Deployments were restarted at 22:09:32Z (ad, payment), those services stopped accepting connections, and frontend's AdService/GetAds and checkout's PaymentService/Charge calls failed, producing the frontend 500s and the RequestErrorRate alert.

Alternative candidate: the 22:09:32Z rollout restart of Deployments ad and payment itself (cold start of the replacement pods, no probes defined) removed the only serving instances and caused the connection refusals; the fault flags may be unrelated coincidence.

The declared fault effects were not observed at the applications themselves: ad logged normal ad responses after 22:18:28Z and payment logged "Transaction complete" after 22:13:22Z, no error logs or error spans appear for ad or payment, and the flags were still on; the only error text observed is connection refused at the ad/payment Service IPs, not an adFailure or paymentFailure application error.

A defect internal to frontend is rejected: every frontend error span examined carries a downstream gRPC error detail (ECONNREFUSED to the ad Service IP on grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, and connection refused to the payment Service IP inside checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge), and frontend's cart, currency, product-catalog and recommendation calls show no error status.

During the error burst the requesting path also failed at frontend-proxy (ingress and router frontend egress spans with http.status_code=500, 0.33 and 0.30 spans/s at 22:20 UTC) and at load-generator (its GET/POST spans with http.status_code=500), i.e. the failures were visible on those entities' own spans.

gaps: The change_history integration is not available, so who or what set kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T22:09:32Z on Deployments ad and payment, and when the flagd-config flag values were changed, could not be verified.

The declared faults themselves were not observed: neither adFailure ("Fail ad service") nor paymentFailure ("100%") produced any ad/payment error span or error log line, and payment completed charges; whether these enabled settings were actually delivered to and applied by the services is unknown.
The Prometheus query for an alerting rule named RequestErrorRate returned no rules (status no_data), so the alert's expression, threshold and evaluation history could not be verified.
A NetworkPolicy query in namespace otel-demo returned no objects, so network-level blocking of ad/payment could not be confirmed or excluded from this query.
The flagd pod (flagd-56d9c6c679-xwgx9) returned no log lines for 22:05-22:20 UTC (status no_data), so its config reload behaviour around 22:09 is unknown.

No previous container instances existed for ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 or payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84, so the terminated old pods' logs are unavailable; a pod-log query for ad over 22:09:30-22:13:00 returned no data, so ad's startup output is unknown.
Frontend error behaviour after 22:21 UTC was not sampled (metric series stop at 22:21), so whether the alert condition has fully cleared is unknown.

Events outside otel-demo were also present (data-recorders Jobs, PVCs, a FailedScheduling Pod and a VolumeFailedDelete PersistentVolume) but no evidence ties them to frontend's errors; they were not investigated further.
next_steps: Consult cluster audit/change history to identify the actor and exact time of the Deployment restarts on ad and payment and of the flagd-config change.

Verify with the OpenFeature/flagd provider whether adFailure and paymentFailure are being delivered and evaluated (e.g. flagd evaluation metrics or per-service flag logs), since the enabled settings were not observed taking effect.
Re-check frontend error rate and the ad/payment span rates for the period after 22:21 UTC to confirm the burst has ended.
Review whether ad and payment should define readiness probes, since their absence let replacement pods receive traffic before listening (connection refused).
